quizData.question: What is the most common formula described for organizing a story into three major sections?
What can correctly applied story organization help ensure in a film or game?
Which act places the audience into the action or drama and aims to capture attention immediately?
Which act focuses on the character's problem and should introduce it immediately?
When can background events leading up to the opening action be introduced?
Which act focuses on obstacles that stand in the way of solving the problem introduced earlier?
Which act usually contains a series of obstacles the character must overcome?
Which act comprises the bulk of dramatic tension in the story?
Which act is reached when the problem introduced at the beginning has been solved?
Which act often requires the character to face and remove the obstacles encountered earlier to reach resolution?
What type of game is given as an example of a satisfying experience that does not necessarily require a storyline?
Which game genre is described as relying heavily on story and sometimes becoming a delivery vehicle for it?
Which five elements are listed as helping turn rough ideas into a preliminary story form?
quizData.answer: premise, backstory, synopsis, theme, and setting
choices: premise, backstory, synopsis, theme, and setting
plot, conflict, realism, focus, and avatar
hero, shadow, mentor, ally, and guardian
self, team, community, society, and humanity

quizData.question: Which element is a one- or two-sentence summary or short paragraph of the game's purpose and overall theme?
Which element often appears on game packaging and is intended to intrigue customers into buying the game?
Which element should focus on what is unique about the game and may indicate its genre while addressing the player directly?
Which element provides information leading up to where the game begins?
Which element may appear as a short paragraph in an instruction manual or as opening text accompanied by a voice-over?
Which element helps orient the player to the game's purpose and action and can help establish initial bonds with certain characters?
Which element or storyline can exist throughout the game itself and involve the player in the setting and actions?
Which element can help a player escape reality, become immersed in an artificial game world, and become emotionally involved with characters?
Which element represents what the story is truly about even when it is not stated explicitly?
Which element usually relates to a primary obstacle faced by the main character or characters?
Which element can be expressed as a defining question such as whether murder is justified or love can triumph?
Which element represents the world explored by the audience, characters, or player?
Which element asks designers to think about the world where characters live and interact, including location, time period, history, and geography?
Which element can draw on traditional media locations such as space for science fiction, a haunted house for horror, or a crime scene for mystery?
Which element is concerned with how the story unfolds rather than what the story is about?
Which element can be part of story structure but can also be dictated by how the game is played?
Which element is a sequence of events that forces increasingly difficult decisions and drives the story toward a climax and resolution?
What storytelling practice maximizes dramatic tension by repeatedly placing the player near disaster and allowing narrow escapes?
Which technique draws players back to the main storyline even while they make choices and have apparent freedom?
Which technique can widen a game's scope through more subquests or by introducing new characters or objects leading into unexplored areas?
Which technique causes players to forget real life and accept an artificial reality created by the game?
Which technique specifically refers to accepting rules and experiences that might not make sense in the real world?
Which technique is illustrated by people flying without air transport or human-looking characters being evil while demons are good?
Which technique contrasts with accepting impossible game rules by mimicking the real world as closely as possible?
Which technique is appropriate when players want reality and authenticity, such as a visually accurate contemporary setting?
Which archetype is the central character in a single-player game and serves as the player's avatar?
Which archetype must be someone the player can identify and bond with?
Which archetype represents the central character's opposite and is often the ultimate evil character?
Which archetype may be the adversary responsible for the central character's problem and can remain hidden until the climax?
Which archetype can represent the dark side of the central character?
Which archetype often guides the central character toward action and provides wisdom from a similar journey?
Which archetype helps the central character progress and can assist with tasks that are difficult or impossible to accomplish alone?
Which archetype blocks progress until the central character has proven worth and therefore acts as a test?
Which archetype could be a henchman or an internal block such as self-doubt, fear, or discomfort?
Which archetype is neutral, enjoys making mischief, and can either cause damage or provide comic relief?
Which archetype facilitates change in the story and provides the central character with direction?
Which character role is the main character whose point of view centers a single-player game?
Which character role must drive the story forward by acting and making things happen rather than simply reacting?
Which character role can be physically or morally strong without always being good and often has a tragic flaw that reflects vulnerability?
Which character role is the opposite of the main story-driving character without necessarily being bad?
Which character role may simply hold opposing political, ethical, or lifestyle views?
What device links two opposing characters when they want the exact same thing, such as a love interest, precious stone, or clan leadership?
What does the linking device between opposing characters make more relevant?
Which antagonist type is an anti-hero who could have been the main character and receives punishment at the end?
Which antagonist type may stir audience empathy but causes innocent deaths and is destroyed in the process?
Which antagonist type is initially believed to be villainous but is later revealed as innocent?
Which antagonist type is common in murder mysteries and crime dramas?
Which antagonist type is larger-than-life, bizarre, sometimes comedic, and may dominate the story because of being more interesting?
Which characters are also called pivotal characters and primarily prevent the main character from walking away?
Which characters can jump-start action, carry out the opposing character's bidding, and bring varied viewpoints?
Which characters can be sidekicks or the opposing character's henchmen?
What two broad types can game-world characters belong to?
What type of game entity is controlled by players?
What is a single controlled character called when one player controls only one?
What can result from the direct connection between a player and a single controlled character?
quizData.answer: assigning a personal identity to the avatar
choices: assigning a personal identity to the avatar

quizData.question: When can identification with a single controlled character become more pronounced?
quizData.answer: when the avatar displays realistic features and actions
choices: when the avatar displays realistic features and actions
when the story has no setting
when there is no dramatic tension

quizData.question: What type of character is not controlled by players and is instead created and controlled by the game's artificial intelligence engine?
Which two elements are identified as significant in developing character relationships and character change?
What forms a powerful three-way relationship among characters in a story?
Which three-way relationship is commonly illustrated by two opposing characters competing for the attention of the same love interest?
What can happen to a character's role when many three-way relationships exist in the same story?
quizData.answer: the role can change based on each triangle
choices: the role can change based on each triangle

quizData.question: What is the process of a central character's growth and development called?
How is a character arc illustrated?
quizData.answer: through behavior rather than monologue or dialogue
choices: through behavior rather than monologue or dialogue

quizData.question: What is identified as the core of character development?
Whose hierarchy-of-needs model is used as the basis for the development levels?
How do the development levels progress in scope?
Which level describes a central character concerned only with personal needs and thoughts?
Which level describes bonding with one other person such as a lover, friend, colleague, or family member?
Which level marks the point where the central character is no longer looking out only for himself or herself but for another character as well?
Which level describes bonding with a small group that shares common interests?
Which level fulfills the need to belong and can be seen when MMOG players form guilds?
Which level occurs when a smaller group becomes part of a larger organized network such as a neighborhood, city, school, or company?
Which level involves self-actualization and spiritual growth after comfort, love, and acceptance have been achieved in a larger group?
